title: Diabetes-friendly nutrition
content: Focus on high-fiber vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains. Limit refined sugars and monitor carbohydrate portions. Pair meals with regular activity and follow your clinician's A1C targets.

title: Blood pressure lifestyle support
content: Reduce sodium intake, maintain healthy weight, limit alcohol, manage stress, and take prescribed medications consistently. Home BP monitoring helps track trends between visits.

title: Asthma trigger awareness
content: Common triggers include allergens, cold air, smoke, and respiratory infections. Use controller medications as prescribed and keep a rescue inhaler accessible. Seek urgent care for severe shortness of breath.

title: Medication adherence
content: Take medications at the same time daily, use pill organizers or app reminders, and never stop prescriptions without consulting your clinician. Report side effects promptly.

title: Allergy safety
content: Avoid known allergens, read food and drug labels carefully, and carry epinephrine auto-injectors if prescribed. Anaphylaxis requires immediate emergency care (call local emergency number).

title: Mental wellness basics
content: Prioritize sleep hygiene, physical activity, social connection, and mindfulness. Persistent mood changes warrant professional evaluation. Crisis lines are available in many regions.

title: Safe physical activity
content: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly plus strength training twice per week when cleared by your clinician. Start gradually if you have chronic conditions.

title: Preventive care
content: Stay current with age-appropriate screenings, vaccinations, and annual wellness visits. Personalized schedules depend on age, sex, family history, and existing conditions.
